text:
Which of the following are the example of double salt?

A. $\mathrm{FeSO}_{4}\cdot (\mathrm{NH}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}\cdot 6\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

B. $\mathrm{CuSO}_{4}\cdot 4\mathrm{NH}_{3}\cdot \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

C. $\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}\cdot \mathrm{Al}_{2}(\mathrm{SO}_{4})_{3}\cdot 24\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

D. $\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{2}\cdot 4\mathrm{KCN}$

Choose the correct answer :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A=\mathrm{FeSO}_{4}\cdot (\mathrm{NH}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}\cdot 6\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ - double salt

B. $\mathrm{CuSO}_{4}\cdot 4\mathrm{NH}_{3}\cdot \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$
$=[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{4}]\mathrm{SO}_{4}\cdot \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ - complex salt

C. $\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}\cdot \mathrm{Al}_{2}(\mathrm{SO}_{4})_{3}\cdot 24\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ - double salt

D. $\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{2}\cdot 4\mathrm{KCN}$ = 
$\mathrm{K}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]$
- complex salt

Option A, $\mathrm{FeSO}_{4}\cdot (\mathrm{NH}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}\cdot 6\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, is a double salt because it is formed by the combination of two different salts: iron(II) sulfate ($\mathrm{FeSO}_{4}$) and ammonium sulfate ($(\mathrm{NH}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$).

Option B, $\mathrm{CuSO}_{4}\cdot 4\mathrm{NH}_{3}\cdot \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, is a complex salt because it contains a central copper ion coordinated to several ammonia molecules.

In this compound, the copper(II) ion $(Cu^{2+})$ acts as the central metal ion, while the four ammonia molecules $(NH_{3})$ act as ligands, coordinating to the copper ion through their lone pairs of electrons. The sulfate ion $(SO_{4}^{2-})$ and water molecules $(H_{2}O)$ are not involved in the coordination sphere and simply crystallize along with the complex.

Option C, $\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}\cdot \mathrm{Al}_{2}(\mathrm{SO}_{4})_{3}\cdot 24\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, is also a double salt, formed by the combination of two different salts: potassium sulfate ($\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$) and aluminum sulfate ($\mathrm{Al}_{2}(\mathrm{SO}_{4})_{3}$).

The 24 water molecules in the formula are not directly involved in the salt formation but instead function to stabilize the crystal lattice by forming hydrogen bonds with the sulfate ions and other water molecules.

Option D, $\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{2}\cdot 4\mathrm{KCN}$, is not an example of a double salt. It is a complex salt, formed by the coordination of iron(II) ions to cyanide ligands and potassium ions.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift

text:
Highest oxidation state of Mn is exhibited in $\mathrm{Mn}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$. The correct statements about $\mathrm{Mn}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$ are

(A) Mn is tetrahedrally surrounded by oxygen atoms.

(B) Mn is octahedrally surrounded by oxygen atoms.

(C) Contains Mn-O-Mn bridge.

(D) Contains Mn-Mn bond.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The correct statements about $\mathrm{Mn}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$ are:

(A) Mn is tetrahedrally surrounded by oxygen atoms.

(C) Contains Mn-O-Mn bridge.


[IMG]


Manganese (Mn) in $\mathrm{Mn}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$ exhibits its highest oxidation state of +7. The oxidation state is the charge an atom would have if the electrons in a chemical bond were shared equally.

In $\mathrm{Mn}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$, the manganese atoms are surrounded by oxygen atoms in a tetrahedral arrangement. This means that each manganese atom is bonded to four oxygen atoms arranged in a pyramid shape. This tetrahedral arrangement of oxygen atoms results in the highest oxidation state for manganese in $\mathrm{Mn}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$.

$\mathrm{Mn}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$ also contains Mn-O-Mn bridges, which are bonds between two manganese atoms through a shared oxygen atom. These bonds help to reinforce the structure of the molecule and contribute to its stability.

It is incorrect to state that Mn is octahedrally surrounded by oxygen atoms or that $\mathrm{Mn}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$ contains a Mn-Mn bond. An octahedral arrangement would consist of six oxygen atoms surrounding a central manganese atom, and a Mn-Mn bond would involve two manganese atoms sharing electrons without an oxygen atom in between. Neither of these are present in $\mathrm{Mn}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$.

text: A solution of $\mathrm{FeCl}_{3}$ when treated with $\mathrm{K}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]$ gives a Prussian blue precipitate due to the formation of :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Iron(III) chloride reacts with potassium hexacyanidoferrate(II) to give a deep blue precipitate:

$4~\mathrm{FeCl}{}_{3}+3\mathrm{K}{}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]\longrightarrow \mathrm{Fe}{}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}_{3}↓+12\mathrm{KCl}$

The precipitate is iron(III) hexacyanidoferrate(II), $\mathrm{Fe}{}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}_{3}$ (Prussian blue), in which four $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ balance three $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{4-}$ ions.

$\mathrm{Fe}{}_{3}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}_{2}$ would need $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$ with $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$, which is not the pair present here.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
Electrons in a cathode ray tube have been emitted with a velocity of 1000 m s${}^{-1}$. The number of following statements which is/are $\mathrm{true}–$ about the emitted radiation is $____________$.

Given : $\mathrm{h}=6\times 10^{-34}\mathrm{J}\mathrm{s},\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}=9\times 10^{-31}\mathrm{kg}$.

(A) The de-Broglie wavelength of the electron emitted is 666.67 nm.

(B) The characteristic of electrons emitted depend upon the material of the electrodes of the cathode ray tube.

(C) The cathode rays start from cathode and move towards anode.

(D) The nature of the emitted electrons depends on the nature of the gas present in cathode ray tube.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The number of true statements about the emitted radiation is 2, i.e. statements (A) and (C).

(A) is True: The de-Broglie wavelength of an electron can be calculated as lambda = h / p, where h is Planck's constant and p is the momentum of the electron. The momentum of an electron with a velocity of 1000 m/s is mv, where m is the mass of an electron. Plugging in the values, we get 

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{e}}=1000\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s};\mathrm{h}=6\times 10^{-34}\mathrm{Js} \\  \\ \mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}=9\times 10^{-31}\mathrm{kg} \\  \\ λ=\dfrac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{mv}}=\dfrac{6\times 10^{-34}}{9\times 10^{-31}\times 1000}=666.67\times 10^{-9}\mathrm{m} \\  \\ =666.67\mathrm{nm} \end{array}$, 

(B) is False : The characteristic of electrons emitted is
independent of the material of the electrodes of 
the cathode ray tube.

(C) is True: In a cathode ray tube, electrons are emitted from the cathode and move towards the anode under the influence of an electric field.

(D) is False: The nature of the emitted electrons does not depend on the nature of the gas present in the cathode ray tube, but rather on the material of the electrodes and the potential difference applied across them.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift

At what pH, given half cell $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}(0.1\mathrm{M})|\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}(0.001\mathrm{M})$ will have electrode potential of 1.282 V? $___________ ($Nearest Integer)

text:
The total number of chiral compound/s from the following is $______________$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A compound is chiral when it has no plane or centre of symmetry.

In 4-benzylidenecyclohexane-1-carboxylic acid, the H/COOH plane at C4 is perpendicular to the H/Ph plane of the exocyclic C=C, as in an allene, so there is no mirror plane and the molecule is axially chiral.

The propan-2-ol $\mathrm{ArO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{OAr}{}^{'}$ carries two different aryloxymethyl groups (a naphthyloxy and a chloronaphthyloxy group), so C2 is a stereocentre and the molecule is chiral.

The tartaric acid drawn in Fischer projection has both OH groups on the same side, so it is the meso form and achiral.

The cyclohexanehexol has the two adjacent OH groups on hashed bonds and the other four on wedges, so a mirror plane passes through the midpoint of the bond joining the two hashed-OH carbons and the midpoint of the opposite bond: achiral.

The methylenecyclopropane-dicarboxylic acid has both COOH groups on the same face (cis), so the plane through the $=\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ carbon and the midpoint of the opposite ring bond is a mirror plane: achiral.

The chiral compounds are the benzylidenecyclohexane acid and the propan-2-ol, a total of 2.

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift
